| [CLAIM-412](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-412.md) v6 | Experience is constituted by interpretive organization, not produced by it: an appropriately organized process in which signals acquire significance for a system is the experience, so whether a system can have experience becomes whether it can sustain that organization | The owner's, U1 and U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-21. | [CLAIM-414](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-414.md) v4 | Matched ordinary trajectories can conceal differences in an interpretation's efficacy, in the allocation of that efficacy, and in the maintenance of its enabling constraints: in two finite constructions, systems that agree under ordinary operation differ in each, and a specified intervention exposes the difference that passive observation of the matched trajectories does not | A10 of the exchange on experience and interpretation, re-run here. Three one-bit systems behave alike when the interpretation is 0. Under an intervention that sets it to 1, the first never acts on it, the second acts at once, and the third acts one step late, because its own interpretation opens the gate. Two two-constraint systems have the same trajectory, (1,1) throughout. A single perturbation runs one into (0,0) and leaves the other restored to (1,1): one maintains its constraints by [CLAIM-395](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-395.md)'s minimal slow–fast closure, the other is reset from outside.
